
Amateur fighters — 4 replies

1. Two ways to use Unlxck (recommended)

Of course mate. Unlxck gives you two options. It can build a personalised strength & conditioning plan around your boxing, goals and schedule, or you can keep your own coach’s programme and just track your training. You can log sessions and sparring, use round timers and check your recovery in one place.

We’re inviting a few fighters to test it free and give feedback.

https://unlxck.com/signup

2. Get an S&C plan

Yeah mate. If you want more structure outside your boxing sessions, Unlxck generates an S&C plan around your training days, equipment and goals, plus your fight date if you have one. You can follow the sessions and edit or swap exercises as needed. Already got a programme? You can use the tracking side instead.

Free beta: https://unlxck.com/signup

3. Already training with a coach

If your coach handles your programme, you don't need to change it. Unlxck lets you log training and sparring, see your session history and check your recovery without generating a plan. You can still build S&C later if you want.

We’re offering free beta access: https://unlxck.com/signup

4. All-round boxing companion

Think of Unlxck as a place to organise your boxing training. Generate your own S&C plan or stick with your coach’s, then log sessions, track sparring and progress, and use the round timer. It works either way.

We’re letting fighters try it free: https://unlxck.com/signup

Professional fighters — 4 replies

1. Keep your coach, track your training (recommended)

Of course mate. Unlxck works alongside your existing coach and programme, not instead of them. You can log training and sparring, track your session history, use built-in round timers and do recovery check-ins. If you ever want extra S&C structure, there’s also a plan-generation option.

We’re giving a few pros free beta access to test it.

https://unlxck.com/signup

2. Sparring and round timer

Yeah mate. If your training is already sorted, Unlxck helps you keep track of it. You get a round timer with automatic work and rest cues, sparring logs for rounds and intensity, and a history of your sessions. No new training plan needed.

Free beta: https://unlxck.com/signup

3. Training load and recovery

Unlxck lets you record what training you did and how hard it felt, alongside sparring and daily recovery check-ins. You can see your recent workload and get readiness guidance while keeping the sessions your coach has set.

We’re offering a small group free access: https://unlxck.com/signup

4. Optional S&C plan

You’ve got two ways to use Unlxck. Keep your current coach’s programme and use it to track training, or have the app generate a personalised S&C plan around your schedule and goals. You can edit or swap exercises in generated sessions too. It’s your call.

Free beta: https://unlxck.com/signup





How to choose a reply

The two product paths are Generate my S&C plan and I already have a coach or plan. These are not locked to amateur or professional status. Lead with the path that matches the fighter, and mention the other as an option.

- General “send details” reply: use #1 for that segment.
- Needs conditioning or fight-camp structure: amateur #2 or professional #4.
- Already has a coach or S&C programme: amateur #3 or professional #1.
- Interested in sparring, timers or recovery: professional #2 or #3.
- Never imply that the app automatically imports a coach’s programme or replaces coaching decisions. Tracking works without an UNLXCK plan. Readiness is guidance, not medical or sparring clearance.
- Avoid promising detailed manual exercise logging until its database migration and deployment are verified. Basic session and sparring logging are the safe claims.

These are for a fighter who has already asked for details. End with the signup link, not another permission question.

## After the signup link — follow-up messages

These apply only after the details and signup link were actually sent. See the pipeline 3B. REPLIES / SIGNUP FOLLOW UPS view for timing and stage. Do not send on a reply/acceptance date alone.
Replied: 3 days after sending link:

Hey mate, just checking you got the beta link. Any issues signing up? Happy to help.
Replied: final, 4 days after the first actual nudge:
Final check mate. If you are still keen to test Unlxck, here is the link again: https://unlxck.com/signup. No pressure either way.
Accepted: 3 days after sending access/onboarding instructions:
Hey mate, were you able to get into Unlxck? If anything is stopping you getting started, let me know.
Accepted: final, 4 days after the first actual nudge:
Quick final check mate. If you still want to try the beta, I can help you get started. No worries if the timing is off.
Activated: feedback, after 4 days:
How have your first few days on Unlxck been? Anything confusing or that you would change?
Activated: final feedback reminder, 5 days after the first request:
Any quick thoughts from testing the app? Even one thing to improve would help. No pressure.

The cold Follow-Ups Sent counter remains separate from warm tracking. After sending the signup link, tick Details Sent; after sending access instructions, tick Onboarding Sent. After each manual warm follow-up, change Signup Nudges Sent or Onboarding Nudges Sent to 1 or 2. After feedback requests, tick Feedback Requested or Feedback Reminder Sent. When the GitHub PR is deployed, the existing server worker automatically records the timestamps. Never type dates manually. Check Instagram and stop on reply, refusal, progress or completed feedback. No DMs are sent automatically.
